title: KV shadowing pressure forecast (experiment sheet) Q1 2027
content:
Purpose:
Run a controlled shadowing experiment to quantify the KV-cache footprint and GPU-side pressure when onboarding a new family of decoder-only 70B models (quantized). Objective is to produce per-region short-term (7d) and medium-term (30d) capacity deltas and a recommended throttling profile for staged rollout.

Executive summary:
- Quick result: enabling KV shadowing for the new model at 30% of production QPS increases regional KV DRAM usage by ~42% and increases GPU mem reservation per shard by ~2.1 GB on average.
- Tail impact: p95 generation latency increases 6-11% under identical QPS due to increased KV cache churn on long-context requests.
- Operational implication: without throttling, high-density regions (us-west1, eu-west1) will hit KV eviction churn and require adding 0.8-1.6 additional GPU nodes per cluster to keep p95 below SLO.

Experiment setup (short):
- Period: 2026-12-20 to 2027-01-05 (controlled replay window + synthetic spike days)
- Traffic source: 20% real traffic shadowed (sampling by hashed-tenant) + 80% synthetic probe mix to stress long-context flows
- Model variants: new-70b-q4_0, new-70b-q4_1 (two quantized variants)
- KV shadowing config: write-shadow enabled, read-shadow disabled for first week, then read-shadow enabled in stage 2
- Measurement buckets: per-region (us-west1, us-east1, eu-west1, ap-southeast1), per-shard, per-model-variant

Key baseline (pre-shadow) metrics (median across warm-days):
Region	QPS	AvgSeq	KV hit%	KV DRAM/region	GPU util(%)	p95(ms)
us-west1	12000	96	78	1.8 TB	62	310
us-east1	8500	74	81	1.1 TB	58	295
eu-west1	7200	88	76	980 GB	60	320
ap-southeast1	2100	120	69	420 GB	54	360

Shadow scenario results (aggregated medians during steady-state shadowing):
Scenario	QPS_frac	KV_hit%	KV DRAM delta	GPU mem delta/shard	GPU util_delta	p95_delta
A - read-shadow off	0.20	77 (-1)	+160 GB (+9%)	+1.0 GB	+3%	+6%
B - read-shadow on	0.20	70 (-8)	+420 GB (+23%)	+2.1 GB	+7%	+11%
C - full traffic emulate	1.00	66 (-12)	+2.1 TB (+117%)	+5.0 GB	+18%	+35%
D - throttled rollout (gradual to 60%)	0.60	72 (-6)	+950 GB (+52%)	+2.8 GB	+9%	+18%

Per-region time-to-saturation heatmap (days until KV churn leads to >15% p95 degradation if no mitigation):
Region	Low(10k QPS)	Med(50k QPS)	High(100k QPS)
us-west1	21	9	4
us-east1	28	12	5
eu-west1	25	10	4
ap-southeast1	45	20	9

Observations and mechanics: 
- KV eviction churn is the primary driver of GPU-side performance regressions. The new model has ~1.9x larger per-request KV bytes due to longer prefix caching needs and denser key spaces from the tokenizer change.
- Read-shadow increases effective working set because the shadow cache is populated parallel to production cache; unless the shadow paths share the same cache entries, we see near-additive DRAM usage.
- On high-concurrency shards, KV lookup latency increases non-linearly when DRAM working set crosses NUMA node boundaries; observed on p4d32 configs when KV > 1.6 TB/region.

Mitigations tested (and quick results):
- Prefetch-window tuning: reducing prefix prefetch depth from 512 tokens -> 256 reduced KV DRAM delta by ~17% with ~2% generation quality cost (measured by eval prompt buckets).
- Shadow read-sampling: enabling read-shadow at 10% reduced DRAM footprint vs full read-shadow by ~65% while still capturing miss patterns for offline analysis.
- Adaptive eviction policy (LRU with time-decay): reduced p95 regression by ~40% in mid-density regions.
- Throttled rollout with canary pinning: 40% -> 60% limit per region gave best cost/quality tradeoff in simulation.

Cost impact estimate (30-day window, projected):
- Baseline infra cost for regions in scope: ~$1.4M/month.
- Scenario B (20% shadow + read-shadow on) adds ~$170k/month in GPU+DRAM cost due to extra nodes and DRAM reservation (model coefficients + instance hour delta).
- Scenario C (full onboard) would roughly double monthly infra cost in affected regions (~+120%).

Recommendations (short):
1) Start rollout using write-shadow only, keep read-shadow off for 14 days while monitoring miss patterns (INFRA-3124).
2) Tune prefetch-window to 256 for new-70b-q4_0 as default; keep q4_1 for latency-sensitive customers.
3) Implement read-shadow sampling at 10% for first four weeks if offline patterns need verification.
4) Enforce per-region rollout caps: 40% by default, auto-increase to 60% only when last-7-day p95 trend < +8% and KV DRAM growth < +20%.
5) Prepare automated scale-up policy: add +1 GPU node per shard when KV DRAM > 1.5 TB or p95 > SLO for >12h.

Action items:
- Priya Nair: finalize rollout flagging logic in infra config and create canary template (due 2027-01-22).
- Ethan Park: add NUMA-aware telemetry for KV lookups to SRE dashboards (due 2027-01-25).
- Marta Silva: run full 30d cost projection for billing impact and update pricing recommendations (due 2027-01-29).
- Ravi Gupta: prototype read-shadow sampling library and add to runtime PR #842 (link above) (due 2027-01-21).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Long-term behaviour of tokenizer-produced key density under high-diversity prompt mix. We need more >30d replay coverage.
- Whether multi-tenant KV aliasing is causing false positives in eviction (initial signs observed; requires tenant-id hashed experiments).

Appendix: raw sample rows (from the synthetic probe set, single-day snapshot):
timestamp	region	model	qps	seq_len	kv_bytes_per_req	kv_hits	kv_dram_region_gb	gpu_mem_reserve_gb	gpu_util	p95_ms
2027-01-09T14:03Z	us-west1	new-70b-q4_0	320	256	34.2 KB	0.71	2320	12.4	69	345
2027-01-09T14:03Z	eu-west1	new-70b-q4_1	210	128	22.6 KB	0.65	1984	11.8	66	362

Notes for reviewers:
- This sheet is an experiment artifact. Numbers are median estimates from mixed real+synthetic replay and have visible variance (see linked CSVs in Confluence page).
- If accepted, these throttles will be encoded as rollout policy templates in the console under product-hosted-api -> rollouts -> canary templates.

Related tickets and references:
